title: The Charlie Brown Condition
author: O. Alan Noble
source: You Are Not Your Own Substack, December 1, 2025
summary: Noble captures the emotional dislocation many experience during holidays: the gap between expected joy and actual feeling. Charlie Brown's lament resonates with those experiencing loss, heartbreak, or seasonal depression. Beneath circumstantial causes lies a deeper issue: the inability to trust God's sovereignty and let go of control. Noble locates the condition in cultural demands to perform emotion and spiritual resistance to leisure. He offers no quick fix but calls readers toward deeper faith in divine love and providential care despite emotional storms.
points: Emotional mismatch between expectations and reality is widespread during holidays.
The inability to feel joy is sometimes rooted in fear of loss.
Cultural pressure to feel happy on schedule prevents authentic emotional honesty.
Trusting God's sovereignty requires surrendering the demand for perfect certainty.
Real faith does not demand emotional perfection but steadfast trust in love.
quotes: I think there must be something wrong with me since Christmas is coming but I am not happy.
I don't feel the way I am supposed to feel during the holidays.
There are a variety of reasons why people struggle to feel the way society expects them to.

A fear of letting go and things going poorly amounts to distrust in God. Even while we are blown about by doubts his love never wavers from us.” Archived from You Are Not Your Own Substack on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
